title: Categorize countries by a name pattern
description:
Write a function `categorize_countries(path, pattern)` that reads the country data JSON file at `path` and returns the names of every country containing `pattern` (case-insensitive), alphabetically sorted.

Uses the real 250-country dataset, unlike the day's own 6-country example list - 'land' alone matches 29 real country names.

hints: Idea to consider: this is the same substring-filter idea as filter_containing, applied to real loaded data

Once the JSON is loaded into a list of country dicts, filtering by whether pattern appears in c['name'].lower() works exactly the same as it did on the small in-memory countries list earlier in this day.
Load the file, keep the names where pattern.lower() is in name.lower(), and return them sorted.
expected_behavior: Returns the alphabetically sorted country names containing pattern.

hidden_tests.expected: ['Afghanistan', 'Kazakhstan', 'Kyrgyzstan', 'Pakistan', 'Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha', 'Tajikistan', 'Turkmenistan', 'Uzbekistan']
hidden_tests.label: 'stan' pattern - also catches 'Tristan' as a substring

explanation: The pattern-matching logic doesn't change between a 6-item list and a 250-item one - only the data source does, which is what reading from a real file rather than a hardcoded list demonstrates.
